input: Learn to read a stock options chain

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Options chains have many components (strike price, expiration, bid/ask, IV, Greeks, open interest, volume). Knowing which parts to focus on determines the depth and breadth of the learning plan.
Whether this is self-study, guided learning with a mentor, or for teaching someone else changes the format and resources recommended.
Whether they plan to trade options actively, hedge existing positions, or just understand financial news changes which skills are most relevant.
How much time they can dedicate per week affects how the learning is paced and structured.
Some people learn best through video, others through reading or hands-on practice with a paper trading account — this shapes the resources recommended.
Knowing what 'done' looks like — e.g., being able to place a real trade, explain a chain to someone else, or pass a knowledge check — determines when the task is complete.
The brokerage or platform they use (or plan to use) determines which specific options chain interface they need to learn to read.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to read a stock options chain
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to develop the ability to understand and interpret a stock options chain, likely for investing or trading purposes.

questions.title: Which parts of the chain do you want to master first?
questions.description: Does the user want a full overview of all components (strike, expiration, bid/ask, Greeks, IV, open interest) or to focus on specific columns most relevant to their immediate goal?

questions.title: What do you intend to do once you can read a chain?
questions.description: Understanding the end goal — actively trading options, hedging a portfolio, or simply understanding financial news — determines which concepts to prioritise.

questions.title: What is your current experience level with options or investing?
questions.description: A complete beginner needs foundational definitions (calls, puts, premium) before tackling a chain, while someone with stock experience can move faster.

questions.title: How much time per week can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: 30 minutes a day versus a few hours on weekends requires very different pacing and resource formats.

questions.title: How do you learn best — videos, reading, or hands-on practice?
questions.description: Preferred learning style determines whether to recommend YouTube courses, written guides, or paper trading platforms for live chain practice.

questions.title: What will make you feel confident that you have truly learned this?
questions.description: The user's definition of success — placing a paper trade, explaining the chain to someone, or consistently identifying good setups — sets the finish line.

questions.title: Which brokerage or trading platform will you use for this?
questions.description: Different platforms (Thinkorswim, Robinhood, Tastytrade, etc.) display options chains differently, so the learning plan should be tailored to a specific interface.
